2.4.2.2 Noise
Existing noise within the project area is limited to natural ambient levels, with the exception of occasional increases during logging operations and other human activities. The Applicant reports that a survey of noise levels of the environment at the site shows a maximum ambient noise level of 70 dBA near the Lower Whitewater Falls, dropping to 50 dBA 600 feet from the falls.
2.5 UNIQUE FEATURES
2.5.1 Scenic and Esthetic Resources
The proposed project area appears very rural in character with little land that could be considered developed. The small portion of so-called developed land consists of South Carolina Route 171, which passes very close to the project boundary (Figure 2-26) and Lake Jocassee that lies in the southeast. There is additional evidence of activity in the numerous logging roads of various types in the project area. In total, they contribute little to the concept of development. The project area can be generally described as mountainous terrain with moderate to steep slopes prevailing (Figure 2-27). The area contains hardwoods and pine with a great deal of laurel and rhododendron throughout (Figure 2-28).
Few of the logging roads in the project area have been made suitable for travel even by four-wheel drive vehicles (Figure 2-29). As a result of limited roads, heavy cover, and generally steep slopes, access is difficult.
Howard, Bad, and West Bad Creeks are small headwater mountain streams within the project area. Flow and channel characteristics indicate that they could generally be classified as the "pool and riffle" type (Figure 2-30). The stream gradients are rather steep with resulting high velocities and turbulent flow condition which vary greatly in rather short distances.
The elements of limited development and access, mountainous terrain, dense cover, and turbulent stream flow provide visual unity and excitement, but little variety to the general character of the project area. Despite this lack of variety, the elements result in an enjoyable scenic resource. Although enjoyable, the area is not unique in character as compared to its surroundings. All of these elements could be found in other stream valleys in the vicinity.
